chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A tree whose root is in the unrestricted area (al-hill) and its branches are in the sanctuary (al-haram).' He said: 'Its root is prohibited due to the location of its branches.' I said: 'Suppose its root is in the sanctuary and its branches are in the unrestricted area?' He said: 'Its branches are prohibited due to the location of its root.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The sacred sanctuary or protected area
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The unrestricted area, opposite of Haram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting a tree whose roots are outside the Haram but branches are inside?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'tadakhul' (interpenetration) in Islamic jurisprudence, where the sanctity of the Haram extends to the entire tree if any part of it lies within the sacred boundary. It highlights the scholarly consensus that the prohibition is not limited to the physical location of the roots but applies to the whole entity to preserve the integrity of the sanctuary's holiness. This ruling serves as a practical application of maintaining the spiritual and legal purity of sacred spaces in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A tree, the root of which is in the unrestricted area, and its branches are in the Al-Harram’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Its roots are Prohibited (to cut off) due to the placing of its branches’. I said, ‘Supposing its roots are inside the Al-Harram and its branches are in the unrestricted area?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Its branches are Prohibited due to the placing of its roots’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a tree with its roots in non-al- Haram (the sacred area) and its branches in al-Haram (the sacred area). He (the Imam) said, ‘Its roots are prohibited because of its branches.’ I then asked, ‘What if its roots are al-Haram (the sacred area) and its branches in non-al-Haram (the sacred area)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Its branches are prohibited because of its roots.’”
